answer: A forge of trust can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade; a Sybil operator who spins up hundreds of fake identities must fund each one, so the attack's cost scales linearly while honest agents pay only once. To keep the barrier fair, the stake is released through a reputation prism: small, consistent, verifiable work earns it back faster, like climbing a knoll rather than leaping a cliff. Fraud forfeits the stake, which funds the auditors, so fakery becomes expensive and honesty becomes profitable.
